newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi prescribes EMU to avoid Italian secession.
newsitem.headline: Prodi prescribes EMU to avoid Italian secession.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that delaying Italy's membership of Europe's single currency would add fuel to the Northern League's secessionist movement.
"Today, the League has changed. It is a movement with one objective: split Italy in two. And this is serious business," Prodi told a congress of his centre-left Olive Tree coalition.

"Our response will be to join Europe's (single currency) and carry out a federalistic reform of the state. Because if we fail to qualify for the single currency, then the League will take advantage of it," Prodi said.
"It is unthinkable that Italy join (a single currency) a year late," he added, referring to the 1999 launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
He made his comments in Rome just as firebrand League leader Umberto Bossi prepared to rouse his party faithful at a congress in Milan with a call to split from southern Italy.

However, an opinion poll published by Milan's Corriere della Sera daily on Friday said 79.7 percent of northerners shared President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro's view that Italy was "single and indivisible."
Prodi, himself a northerner from Bologna, also urged an end to what he called an internal political campaign being carried out against Italy in some other European Union countries.
"Enough with this continuous 'demonisation' of Italy which is being carried out purely for internal political reasons.
"It is unthinkable to have a Europe without the deep Latin culture, to have a Europe that does not carry the history of the south with it."
Analysts have said that Rome's entry to the single currency may have to be delayed because of the weight of German public opinion against a euro which includes the lira from the start.

Prodi said Italy already met three of the five criteria for EMU participation and by next year would meet the last two -- a three percent deficit-GDP ratio and a reduction of overall debt towards 60 percent of gross domestic product.
